newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast distillates stay weaker with "racks".
newsitem.headline: US West Coast distillates stay weaker with "racks".

text.p: Ample supplies and lower "rack" prices have pushed down U.S. West Coast middle distillate prices Wednesday, continuing a trend that saw CARB diesel off eight percent from last week, traders said.
CARB diesel in Los Angeles fell two cents to 63/64 cents a gallon Wednesday, an eight-cent-drop from early last week.
Ample distillate stocks, which stood 1.1 million barrels over year-ago, prompted refiners like Atlantic Richfield Co. to drop prices at distrbution terminals, or "racks," traders said.
"Middle distillates have been very weak today," one broker said.
Racks have fallen seven cents to 67 cents the last week.
That prompted wholesale prices, which feed terminals, to fall as well.
Low sulphur diesel dropped 1.50 cents a gallon from Tuesday to 63.50/64.50 cents.
Unleaded gasoline for sale in California (CARB) fell one cent during the day to 67/68 cents a gallon, in line with a 23-cent-a-barrel fall in crude oil for June delivery today.
The lower futures prices also pushed down conventional gasoline by 1.50 cents a gallon to 63.50/64.50 cents.
